# Results — Study 718 (Forbes-Billionaire-Drift)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The question — **"when a
founder is newly minted onto the Forbes billionaires list, buy the vehicle?"** — tested as
a textbook short-window **event study**: around each annual-list publication date, the
**cumulative abnormal return** (CAR) is the stock's return minus a **market-model** fit
(`stock = α + β·benchmark`) estimated on a clean pre-list window, cumulated over the event
window. Forbes does not license a machine-readable "new entrants" feed, so events come from
a **hardcoded, cited table** of ~27 newly-minted-founder vehicles. Offline core + synthetic
control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — each event ticker + SPY + QQQ (public, no key) |
| Event table | hardcoded `FORBES_EVENTS` (ticker, founder, list year, list date), fingerprint **42d8908759c9** |
| As-of | 2026-07-12 |
| Events in table | **27**; with usable price history **25** (LAZR/Luminar & NKLA/Nikola dropped — delisted/renamed after collapse) |
| Benchmark / model | market model `stock = α + β·SPY` (primary), 60-day estimation window, 5-day gap; QQQ as the tech-beta cross-check |
| Windows | **pre** [−63,−1] (the run-up), **announce** [0,+2] (list days), **post** [+1,+63] (the tradable drift — headline) |
| Entry / costs | tradable variant enters **1 day after** publication; one-way 20-bps round-trip |

> **Two named caveats (on the Signal axis).** (1) **Survivorship, and it points against the
> believers.** The two flashiest fresh-billionaire vehicles — **Nikola** (Trevor Milton, later
> a fraud conviction) and **Luminar** (Austin Russell) — imploded and dropped off the tape, so
> the surviving 25-name post-list mean is biased **upward**; the real trade included two names
> that went toward zero. (2) The **"newly-minted" label** is Forbes' own framing (first
> appearance on the annual list) and, for a hand-compiled sample, a judgement call at the
> margin (paper-billionaire pre-IPO vs. first tradable appearance). Neither moves the verdict:
> it rests on the *reverse causality* (the run-up is why they made the list) and the
> *beta artifact* (the drift is tech beta, not alpha), both robust.

## The three windows — where the "effect" actually lives (market model, SPY benchmark)

| window | what it measures | n | mean CAR | win-rate | *t* vs 0 | placebo *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **pre** [−63,−1] | the run-up *before* the list | 25 | **+5.66%** | 80% | **+3.02** | 0.003 |
| **announce** [0,+2] | the list-day repricing | 25 | **−2.98%** | 28% | **−2.81** | 0.016 |
| **post** [+1,+63] | the **tradable** post-list drift | 25 | **+12.42%** | 68% | **+1.70** | 0.108 |

Read it carefully. The two windows that clear |*t*| = 2 are the **wrong** ones for the
believers: the **pre-list run-up** (+5.66%, *t* = 3.02) is pure **selection / look-ahead** —
that run-up is *why* the founder made the list, and you could only have "traded" it by knowing
the future roster; and the **list-day reaction is negative** (−2.98%, *t* = −2.81) — a
**sell-the-news** dip on the coronation, and un-tradable in your favour. The one window the
believers need — the holdable **post-list drift** — is **+12.42% but *t* = 1.70** (placebo
*p* = 0.108): it **fails** the *t* ≥ 2 bar.

## The post-list "drift" is a beta artifact, not alpha

| how the post-list [+1,+63] CAR is measured | mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| market model vs **SPY** (broad market) | **+12.42%** | +1.70 |
| market model vs **QQQ** (tech/growth) | **+7.70%** | +1.09 |
| plain **excess over SPY** (implicit β = 1, no fit) | **+1.46%** | **+0.22** |

These are freshly-IPO'd, ultra-high-beta growth names, and a 60-day market-model beta on them
is unstable. Strip the fitted beta and just difference the stock against the market (β = 1) and
the "drift" is **+1.46% at *t* = 0.22 — indistinguishable from zero.** Benchmark against the
tech ETF the beta was really tracking (QQQ) and it falls to +7.70% (*t* = 1.09). The impressive
SPY number is the **growth factor SPY doesn't hedge plus market-model beta noise** — not a
"billionaire glow."

## The tradable version — enter the day after, net of costs

| trade | mean CAR | *t* | net @ 20 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| buy at first close after publication, hold [+1,+63] | **+12.42%** | +1.70 | +12.22% |
| enter **+1 more day** (lag 1), hold [+2,+64] | +14.31% | +1.94 | +14.11% |

Cost is *not* the binding constraint (these are liquid names, 20 bps barely dents a 3-month
hold) — but neither variant clears *t* = 2, both live inside the placebo cloud, and both are
the SPY-beta artifact above. The per-name dispersion is enormous: post-list outcomes run from
**−64%** (SNAP 2018) to **+85%** (RIVN 2022), so any single-name "buy the vehicle" bet is a
coin flip with fat tails on both sides.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, ~25 high-vol events are weak

A deterministic per-event abnormal-return panel (25 events, high beta + high idiosyncratic
vol to mimic fresh IPOs) with a **plantable post-list drift edge**:

| planted post-list drift | post mean CAR | post *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** (no edge) | +6.03% | **+0.86** |
| **+3000 bps** (+30%/event, enormous) | +36.03% | **+5.14** |

With **no** planted edge the test stays below *t* = 2 (a +6% *point estimate* on 25 ultra-vol
events is still *t* < 1 — exactly the trap the real +12.42% at *t* = 1.70 falls into). Only an
**implausibly large** +30%/event planted drift drives *t* to 5.1. The control proves both
things at once: the engine recovers a real edge when one exists, **and** two dozen high-vol
events are far too weak to certify any post-list edge of plausible size.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The believers' holdable post-list drift is **+12.42% but *t* = 1.70**
  (placebo *p* = 0.108) — it **fails** the *t* ≥ 2 bar — and it **dissolves** once tested
  honestly: **+1.46% (*t* = 0.22)** as a plain excess over the market, **+7.70% (*t* = 1.09)**
  against the tech benchmark. The only effects that clear |*t*| = 2 are the pre-list run-up
  (+5.66%, *t* = 3.02 — pure selection you can't trade) and a **negative** list-day dip
  (−2.98%, *t* = −2.81). There is no tradable "buy the fresh billionaire" edge.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No holdable, benchmark-robust drift to capture; you would be
  buying survivor-selected high-beta names into a −3% coronation dip, with per-name outcomes
  from −64% to +85%, while the two biggest fresh-billionaire vehicles of the era (**Nikola**,
  **Luminar**) went toward zero and off the tape entirely. What's left is tech beta you could
  buy for one QQQ ticket.
- **"Billionaire glow?" — MISATTRIBUTED.** The apparent drift is the **run-up that earned the
  listing** (reverse causality: the stock didn't rise because they made the list; they made
  the list because it rose) **plus tech beta plus the survivors** — not a coronation glow. The
  coronation itself is a small, real, un-tradable *negative*.
